paper.title: Hierarchy-boosted funnel learning for identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes a hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework that integrates unsupervised and supervised learning to efficiently identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL), circumventing large-scale brute-force ab initio calculations. It uses unsupervised clustering on descriptors from the Materials Project database to narrow the search space, performs low-cost high-throughput calculations (PET model) on selected clusters to label κL, and trains an interpretable CatBoost classifier to predict ultralow κL, revealing new structural descriptors governing anharmonicity.

tasks.task_name_raw: identifying semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity
tasks.objective: Identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL) for potential thermoelectric applications.
input_requirements: descriptors derived from Magpie and Voronoi tessellations
output_goal: list of candidate semiconductors with ultralow κL

evidence.text: Here, we propose a novel hierarchy-boosted funnel learning (HiBoFL) framework, which is successfully applied to identify semiconductors with ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κL).
We then apply this HiBoFL framework to efﬁciently identify semiconductors with ultralow κL as shown in Fig. 1b.
Materials with κPET not exceeding 2 W/mK are labeled as 1, which are considered to possess ultralow κL; otherwise, they are labeled as 0, signifying non-ultralow κL.

stages.stage_name_raw: obtaining material dataset from Materials Project database
stages.stage_goal: Acquire initial theoretical dataset of semiconductors for screening.

evidence.text: Initially, we start by acquiring all the materials from the MP database based on its API, resulting in a total of 1,54,718 entries saved in a JSON ﬁle as the Python dictionary object.

stages.stage_goal: Filter materials to generate first-level dataset satisfying thermodynamic, electronic, and computational constraints.

evidence.text: Ultimately, through excluding the materials containing hydrogen, lanthanides, and actinides, and conducting structural analysis, we further obtain 2675 three-dimensional (3D) crystal structures without calculation errors. These materials constitute the first-level dataset for our in-depth investigations.

stages.stage_name_raw: unsupervised learning for clustering materials with similar κL
stages.stage_goal: Group materials into clusters based on composition and structure descriptors to identify problem-specific clusters likely to contain ultralow κL materials.
stage_output: problem-specific clusters C1 and C2 (704 materials)

evidence.text: K-means clustering41,42 is then employed to identify materials with similar κL, which is visualized in a low-dimensional space using t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE)43, and problem-speciﬁc clusters are selected based on similarity design rules to form the second-level dataset.

Since the materials with a high likelihood of possessing relatively low κL tend to group into the two clusters of C1 and C2, the exploration scope for ﬁnding materials with low κL is reduced from 2675 materials to 704 materials, narrowing by approximately three-quarters. As a result, these two problem-speciﬁc clusters (C1 and C2) further constitute our second-level dataset.

stages.stage_name_raw: high-throughput calculation of κL using PET model
stages.stage_goal: Assign κL labels to materials in problem-specific clusters via low-cost empirical modeling.
stage_output: local database of 661 materials with κPET values at 300 K

evidence.text: We use the phonon-elasticity-thermal (PET) model44 to perform low-cost HTC on the materials in the second-level dataset, establishing a local database based on the HTC results.

stages.stage_name_raw: statistical analysis and candidate screening from local database
stages.stage_goal: Analyze κPET distribution to recommend TE candidates and select specific materials for in-depth mechanism analysis.
stage_input: local database of 661 materials with κPET
stage_output: list of candidate materials with κPET ≤ 2 W/mK (Table S2)
Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2GeSe3 selected for first-principles validation

evidence.text: These materials also constitute a list of candidate materials with potential applications in the TE ﬁeld (Table S2), which undoubtedly prove that the problem-speciﬁc clusters we identiﬁed through unsupervised learning indeed contain a signiﬁcant number of materials with low thermal conductivity.

To further validate the results and conduct in-depth analysis of the phonon thermal transport mechanisms, we calculate more precise κL values according to ﬁrst-principles derived force constants and Boltzmann transport theory for the unreported materials Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2GeSe3, which are screened out based on the formula type ranking among the materials with the lowest κPET values.

stages.stage_name_raw: first-principles validation of κL for selected candidates
stages.stage_goal: Validate κPET predictions and reveal phonon transport mechanisms via accurate ab initio calculations.
stage_output: phonon dispersion, PDOS, spectral κL(ω), group velocity, lifetime

evidence.text: To further validate κPET from the PET empirical equation and investigate the phonon thermal transport mechanisms, we calculated more accurate κL values for Cs2SnSe3 and Cs2SnSe3 by iteratively solving the phonon BTE94,97

Figure 4e depicts the calculated κL as the function of temperature ranging from 100 to 500 K at different axes in the discussed two semiconductors... Moreover, these materials all exhibit intrinsically ultralow κL, with values all below 0.25 W/mK in any direction at 300 K, signiﬁcantly lower than the κL (~2.3 W/mK) of the traditional TE material PbTe71.

stages.stage_name_raw: training CatBoost classifier for ultralow κL prediction
stages.stage_goal: Train supervised classification model on labeled local database to directly predict ultralow κL.
stage_input: local database (661 materials with κPET labels)

evidence.text: In the fourth step, we perform ensemble learning on the labeled local database for directly classifying ultralow κL, training a robust CatBoost classifier45.

stages.stage_goal: Assess classification accuracy and robustness using standard metrics.

evidence.text: As a result, the performances of the optimal CatBoost classiﬁcation model are characterized by the ROC curve and the confusion matrix (Fig. 6b), showing its great ability in classifying semiconductors with ultralow κL due to the high ROC AUC (0.94), accuracy (0.90), precision (0.89), recall (0.90) and F1-score (0.89).

stages.stage_name_raw: interpretable analysis using SHAP to uncover κL modulation mechanisms
stages.stage_goal: Reveal physical meaning of key descriptors and discover new factor (Lmin) governing structural anharmonicity.
stage_output: discovery of Lmin as special descriptor influencing phonon lifetime

evidence.text: We propose that the ratio of these two terms, i.e., Lmin, might potentially reﬂect the anharmonicity of materials. Lower Lmin values exhibit positive SHAP values, which favor the emergence of ultralow κL.
